properties.summary: Environmental Health & Safety violation issued on 10/23/2024 to SENECA RESOURCES CO LLC in Middlebury Township, Tioga county. 78a66(b)1 - REPORTING AND REMEDIATING SPILLS AND RELEASES – Reporting releases – Operator or other responsible party failed to report spills and releases of regulated substances to the Department.
properties.content:
Report Details
Inspection Client: SENECA RESOURCES CO LLC
Violation Type: Environmental Health & Safety
Violation Date: 10/23/2024
Violation Code: 78a66(b)1 - REPORTING AND REMEDIATING SPILLS AND RELEASES – Reporting releases – Operator or other responsible party failed to report spills and releases of regulated substances to the Department.
Violation ID: 8205476
Permit API: 117-22231
Unconventional: Yes
County: Tioga
Municipality: Middlebury Township
Inspection Type: Administrative/File Review
Inspection Date: 10/23/2024
Comments: On 10/23/2024, DEP representative John Rogers conducted an admin inspection for the Seneca Resource's Taft 851 well site located in Middlebury Township, Tioga County. This inspection is to report the results of three water samples that were collected during fracking operations from three different locations at the site. During inspections #3846615 and #3846665, conducted on 10/2/2024 and 10/3/2024; the department discovered instances of elevated conductance fluid on the north side of the pad surface and in the sediment basin below the north side of the pad. Samples were collected on 10/3/2024. On 10/19/2024, the department received the results of the samples. Sample 9551-142 was collected from the south of two puddles of water near the outfall at the center of the north perimeter berm; both puddles field tested at 19.99 mS conductance. The upper limit for conductivity on the Altair PCTS5 is 19.99 mS. The south puddle measured 6' x 1.5' x 3 inches and the north puddle measured 10' x 3' x 2". The 16" freshwater pipeline and the 16" frac water pipeline traveled through these puddles. There was a multi-colored crusty sheen and the water left a brown film on the sample bottles. The results are shown in pictures 1-3.Sample 9551-143 was collected from within MRC basin 1 in a water/muddy area where the outfall from the center of the north perimeter berm flows into the basin. Water in this area field tested at 16.92 mS conductance. The results are shown in pictures 4-6. Sample 9551-144 was collected from within MRC basin 1, next to the east basin overflow. Water in this area field tested at 1.595 mS conductance. The results are shown in pictures 7-8.The samples show elevated levels of aluminum, iron, manganese, chlorides and strontium which indicates the release of a pollutional substance on the pad and reaching the basin.The release of an unknown volume of elevated conductance fluid to the pad surface and into the sedimentation basin constitutes violations of SWMA 301, CSL 402, 25 PA Code 78a.56(a) and 78a.66(b)(2). This incident does not meet the discharge requirements under 25 PA Code 78a.60(b). Because of the large volume of elevated conductance fluid discovered on the pad surface and in the sedimentation basin, the DEP recommends pursuing Act 2. The DEP recommends the following: 1. The department recommends that Seneca determine the source of the elevated conductance, aluminum, iron, manganese, strontium and chlorides in the water sample and take measures to address it, including but not limited to; ceasing discharge, collecting the water for reuse/disposal, etc.2. Assess the area of elevated conductance fluid at the north side of the pad and the basin; clean/report as necessary.

Report Details

Person stored, transported, processed, or disposed of residual waste inconsistent with or unauthorized by the rules and regulations of DEP.
Violation ID: 862180
Permit API: 015-20889
Unconventional: Yes
County: Bradford
Municipality: Stevens Twp
Inspection Type: Incident- Response to Accident or Event
Inspection Date: 2019-09-09
Comments: On 09/07/19 at 1130 hrs, Steve Moyer notified Phone Duty Officer (Andrew Hobbins)reporting that two puddles on the GU-J-Pad well pad surface tested high for conductivity while removing containment. The first puddle measured approximately 11mS/cm and the other puddle measured 3-4 mS/cm. Mr. Moyer reported that containment cleanup was ongoing, but currently the impacted pad surface is limited to a 30 foot by 40 foot area near the well heads, and a second area is still being investigated is ranging up to 7 mS/cm conductivity and is roughly 50 feet by 60 feet.  Mr. Moyer attributed the high conductivity to a hole somewhere in the containment liner, but no holes were found. A vac truck removed the puddles from the pad surface. Resource Environmental was contracted to delineate the impacted area and do remediation work. SWN finished their drill out and was currently setting up to hook up flow lines for the new wells. No waterways or stormwater/infiltration areas were affected. On September 09, 2019 Department representative Jared Jacobini (Water Quality Specialist) conducted a site inspection in response to an incident reported on 09/07/19 by Steve Moyer (Southwestern Energy (SWN) Regulatory Supervisor) at SWNs WELL PAD J. Also present for the inspection was production supervisor Mike Deming of SWN. When I arrived onsite, the operator had scraped excavated impacted soils near the well cellars and towards the low area on the pad near the level spreader (Photo # 1-8). The excavated soil had been removed and placed into seven roll offs and was being removed during the inspection. At the time of inspection, the volume and cause of the release was not know but was still being investigated with anticipation of pursuing Act 2. The pad surface was screened with a soil probe conductivity meter and a handheld conductivity meter throughout the impacted and excavated area, puddles, and outside of the pad below the level spreader. In one location that did not appear to have been excavated, the soil conductivity was 3.43 mS/ cm (Photo # 9-10). In a second location beyond the well heads along the western pad border a puddle exhibiting a sheen had a conductivity of 1,126 µS/cm (Photo # 12). Mike Deming said that he would have the area were soil conductivity was high scraped up and the location of puddled water vacuumed up. This release should be remediated in accordance with Chapter 78a66(c). As a result of the presence of a pollutional substance discovered on the pad surface the following violations are being cited.

During this inspection, the area of the discovered release was inspected. All fluids within the area were field measured for electrical conductivity and returned readings ranging from 210 to 240us/cm. Impacted solid materials recovered during the cleanup are stored onsite in a lined and covered container (photo #6). Violations cited against API #015-23116 on 4/24/2026 will remain outstanding until attainment with Act 2 standards are met. I departed the site at 1320 hours.

Code Section 78.73(c).
Violation ID: 972183
Permit API: 063-31807
Unconventional: No
County: Indiana
Municipality: Grant Twp
Inspection Type: Administrative/File Review
Inspection Date: 10/17/2022
Comments: EPA Mechanical Integrity Test was conducted on 10/12/2022 at 09:58. Tubing pressure at commencement of test was 2225 p.s.i. Tubing annulus was filled with freshwater and pressured up to 800 p.s.i. MIT concluded at 10:28. Final pressure on tubing annuls was 800 p.s.i. Final pressure on tubing was 2225 p.s.i. Annulus of surface casing was monitored while the pressure test was underway, for any changes in the rate of bubbling. There were no abnormalities observed, indicating there is zonal isolation between the downhole injection zone, and the top-hole freshwater protection zones. The well has passed EPA's mechanical integrity test. PGE's remediation plan proposes the use of a resin material, with gas blocking capabilities. The resin will be pumped into the annular space of the surface casing at a depth of approximately 350', or the cap rock nearest this depth. This depth is determined to be below the deepest fresh groundwater in the area. It is anticipated that by placing the resin at this depth, the cap rock will be restored, thereby preventing the gas from permeating the micro-annulus that is allowing the gas to flow to surface. The resin has been used in similar annular gas scenarios, with success. An alternative procedure of pumping cement into the annular space has been discussed, but the outcome of this procedure is often times unpredictable, and could leave the casing integrity in a compromised condition. PGE anticipates that the resin will be available to them in April, of 2023. The product is currently in short supply, and the available stock has been allotted to other customers.

Unconventional: Yes
County: Lycoming

Inspection Type: Incident- Response to Accident or Event
Inspection Date: 7/29/2026
Comments: This inspection was conducted in response to a notification from the operator that a release of an estimated 20 gallons of produced fluid was released to the pad surface on 7/28/26 at 0244. The notification stated that the fluid was sucked up the same day and impacted soil was excavated and containerized. Work crews were rigging down the drilling rig and associated drilling equipment during this inspection. It rained steadily during this inspection and there was a large volume of stormwater on the pad surface. I met with company man John Hulsey upon arriving on the well pad. He told me that the release occurred in the area of the drilling mud tanks when a jet vac leaked and caused produced fluid to be released to the surface of the pad. I inspected the pad surface and secondary containment for the drilling mud tanks. The fluid on the containment had an electrical conductivity (EC) of 288 uS/cm. The fluid on the pad surface immediately adjacent to the containment berms had an EC of 272 uS/cm. Puddles farther away from the containment on the pad surface had similar readings with none greater than 400 uS/cm. Puddles of stormwater on other areas of the well pad had EC readings of less than 300 uS/cm for each puddle measured. No evidence of produced fluid was observed on the pad surface. The well site secondary containment appeared to be in good condition. No holes were observed in the containment liner.Violations noted against well permit 081-22059 and are considered immediately corrected.

The ground appears to be seeded in most areas, but 70% uniform vegetation has not been achieved at this time. Vegetative growth may be hindered by the amount of rock and gravel on site. The Department recommends the Operator take necessary measures to ensure 70% uniform vegetative growth is achieved for restoration of the site. Based on today's inspection, violations shall remain outstanding.The transmission of this inspection is delayed due to an IT error.

Violations are being issued for accelerated erosion on the access road.

No leaks, spills, or releases observed at the well head at this time.Gas Production Unit (GPU) is surrounded by secondary containment. Fluid is observed within the secondary containment and two cracks are observed along the concrete curb of secondary containment (Photos 3-6) with wet spots observed outside of the secondary containment in the area of the cracks. properties.content:
Report Details
Inspection Client: REPSOL OIL & GAS USA LLC
Violation Type: Environmental Health & Safety
Violation Date: 3/03/2025
Violation Code: CSL 402(b) - POTENTIAL POLLUTION - Conducting an activity regulated by a permit issued pursuant to Section 402 of The Clean Streams Law to prevent the potential of pollution to waters of the Commonwealth without a permit or contrary to a permit issued under that authority by the Department.
Violation ID: 8223194
Permit API: 117-22227
Unconventional: Yes
County: Tioga
Municipality: Covington Township
Inspection Type: Routine/Complete Inspection
Inspection Date: 3/03/2025
Comments: This inspection was conducted in response to a notification from the operator that a fluid was released from secondary containment on the well pad and it flowed off of the well pad. Upon arriving on location I met with Repsol representative Roy Trimmer. He showed me where the fluid peaked out of the containment, down the pad side slope, and along a vegetated infiltration berm. The secondary containment is present along the west side of the well pad. The secondary containment had previously held a battery of upright tanks containing produced fluid. The tanks have been removed from the location and a crew was working to remove the secondary containment during this inspection. The leak in the containment occurred along the west side of the containment near the southwest corner of the pad. The fluid ran down the west pad side slope near the southwest corner of the pad and along a vegetated, earthen infiltration berm. The fluid ran along the toe of the berm. The berm ends at an infiltration basin. The soil was moist along the path of the fluid. The fluid appeared to stop at the rock-lined entrance to the basin. Fluid present in the infiltration basin near the area of the leak along the west side of the containment had electrical conductivity (EC) readings between 1392 uS/cm to 1500 uS/cm as measured by the Oakton water EC meter. The EC readings in the soil on the Hanna soil EC meter were 2070 uS/cm at the highest not far from the toe of the pad side slope to 250 uS/cm where the path of the fluid ended at the entrance to the infiltration basin. Repsol representative Andrew Senefelder arrived on location during this inspection. He told me that their consultant Resource Environmental would be taking soil samples from the path of the fluid as well as a water sample from inside the secondary containment. He said that due to the EC readings in the soil, they did not anticipate finding any exceedances in the soil; however, as a precaution, Repsol plans to scrape the soil along the flow path of the fluid release anyway, he stated.Mr. Senefelder then left and I took sample 0718-253 from the fluid within the secondary containment near where the leak occurred near the southwest corner of the well pad. The sample was sent to the state laboratory the next day to be analyzed for SAC 942 plus Al, Sr, and Br.Due to the unknown spill volume, the Department recommends pursuing Act 2 remediation. In a phone call with PA DEP Water Quality Specialist Supervisor Sean VanFleet on 3/3/25 at 1600, Repsol representative Kris Perritt committed to pursuing Act 2 remediation for this release. Violations noted.

Comments: On August 7, 2025, the Department conducted a Follow Up Inspection of Burnett Oil Co Inc's Stickle Ross Mountain Unit 1H well (129-28648) located in Fairfield Township, Westmoreland County following IR 4011505, where the Department observed several areas of the graveled well pad to have an oily substance on it, specifically in areas relating to the reported re-plugging of the 129-28648 well. Accompanying during today's inspection is Monona Operator/Land Owner Tom Stickle and Plants and Goodwin's Representative Jim Watson.Burnett Oil representative Walter Glasgow stated in an email to the Department (documented in IR 4029448), that clean up began on 7/28/25 and was completed on 7/31/25, once the Department conducts an inspection of the site to determine if all contaminated material was removed, Burnett will replace the removed rock from the graveled well site. Once Waste Management disposes of the contaminated material, Burnett Oil will provide the Department with a quantity of the release. At the time of this inspection, the Department observed an Act 9 sign at the access road entrance to not be in compliance and inside the on-site mailbox was an outdated Emergency Response Plan (ERP). Violations associated with the Act 9 Sign and the ERP are addressed under a separate inspection for 129-28411. An access road was observed to be stabilized with gravel and the perimeters of the well site were observed to be exhibiting greater than 70% uniform and adequate vegetative cover with no erosion or sedimentation issues observed.At the time of this inspection, the 1H: 129-28648 well appeared to be plugged and all plugging equipment appeared to be removed from the well site. A new monument and vent pipe which was reportedly approved by the Department was observed to be installed. The monument was observed to have the plugged well's permit number and replug date posted on it. No fluid leaks or fluid discharges were observed coming from or near this plugged well.At the time of this inspection, the Department observed the graveled well pad to be scraped in the areas that were previously observed to have an oily substance during IR 4013514. At the time of this inspection, the Department did not observe an oily or shiny brown substance anywhere on the graveled well pad. Mr. Watson stated that all contaminated material was placed in the roll off dumpster observed on site, that new gravel will be laid in the release areas and the contaminated material will be properly disposed of following this inspection. The Department requested a waste manifest for the disposed contaminated material be provided to the Department upon its receipt to verify whether the release was less than 42 gallons, and therefore remediated applicably under 78a.66(c)(1). If the quantity of the release is over 42 gallons, the Department recommends the Operator follow the Act 2 guidelines for remediation as set by 78a.66(c)(2).Based on today's inspection, violations issued for an oily substance on the graveled well pad shall remain outstanding at this time pending the receipt of a waste manifest and a quantity of the release.

Unconventional: Yes

Inspection Date: 11/17/2023
Comments: On 11/17/23 an incident inspection of the Coastal Greene Well Site was conducted in response to the report of a spill received by the Department on 11/17/23. Background:On 11/17/23 Greylock self-reported a brine release on the Coastal Greene Well pad. On 11/17/23 I spoke to Keith Eighmey of Greylock to acquire additional details about the spill. During the inspection it was determined that an estimated 10-15 barrels of impaired water had been released to the pad surface from a failure of the 8MH GPU unit. Investigation showed that the release was contained to the pad area and no water ways were impacted. Mr. Eighmey said that Greylock would have equipment, a containment, and a roll off box on site by 1-2pm on 11/17/23. Findings:-An act 9 sign was present at the entrance to the well site (Photo #1).-The spill is suspected to have originated from the 8MH GPU units (Photo #2,6).-Standing water and a wet spot was observed around the GPU units (Photos #2,3,5,6,8,9).-Elevated conductivity was observed in standing water around the GPU units (Photo #4,7). -Crews were present on-site working to repair the GPU units. (Photos #2-6). -No elevated conductivity was observed outside of the spill area.No impacts to WoC were observed. Violations of 78a57(a), SWMA 301, 78a54, and 78a64(a)b are being issued for the release of brine to the ground and failure to have the GPU units in secondary containment for a well drilled in 2018.

Permit API: 033-25738
Unconventional: No
County: Clearfield

Inspection Type: Routine/Complete Inspection

Comments: Routine site inspection on May 7, 2026 with DEP representatives Sue Herzing, Justin Galioto, and John Salinkas. The well appears active and capable of producing. Approximately 30 BBL of brine fluids were measured in the 100 BBL brine tank. Flakey paint and corrosion was observed on the production equipment and axillary pipes. The Department recommends monitoring the equipment and repainting or replacing the equipment if needed. A 5x Altair gas meter was used to screen around the production equipment. No combustible or methane gases were detected. Please note, during the inspection and area of exposed soil (~2'x4') was observed to the right of the brine tank (photos 3-4). I screened the exposed soils and elevated readings were observed with 2.01 mS/cm being the highest reading (photos 5-9). A soil sample was collected 3442-976 and sent to the Departments Lab in Harrisburg and will be tested for SAC 530 plus bromide, lithium, and strontium. While onsite, we contacted Dannic Energy well tender Rob Yohe via phone. Rob was in the area and met us onsite. Rob explained that when he arrived onsite Monday, May 4, 2026, he found that the dump line coming off the well head had corroded off where it connects to top portion of the brine tank and was lying on the ground. The other section remained attached to the well head. He explained that he removed the pipe. He noted, that the well was shut in when he found the dump line lying on the ground. Rob stated that only residual fluids were in the dump line. I explained to Rob, that elevated soils were discovered and that these impacted soils will need to be removed. I contacted Dan Sinclair and left him a voice message regarding my findings. Rob hand excavated impacted soils based off visual impacts to the soil (photos 11-12). I recommended that he cover the excavated area with plastic. The Department recommends screenings the excavated area. Screenings need to be <1.00 mS/cm before being backfilled.Violations have been cited for the brine release. The Department recommends cleaning up spill in accordance with "Addressing Spills and Releases at Oil and Gas Well Sites or Access Roads (800-5000-001).

Comments: On 5/26/2026, the Department conducted an at the former location of the Holchin 2 well site in North Union Township, Fayette County. This inspection follows-up to IR 4181294, where no Rock Construction Entrance (RCE) was installed at the site entrance per the Erosion and Sedimentation (E and S) control plan. In response, violations were issued for failure to failure to follow the E and S plan.An NOV Response to IR 4181294 was requested from the operator by 4/30/2026. However, no response of any kind to IR 4181294 has been received from the operator at the time of this inspection. The Department issued an Order to Diversified (#445705) on August 15, 2025. According to the Order, Diversified is to restore the Well Sites within nine (9) months of Well plugging in accordance with Section 3216 of the 2012 Oil and Gas Act, 58 Pa. C.S. 3216. According to Department records, this well was plugged on 4/08/2026, therefore the site shall be fully restored by 1/08/2027 in accordance with current regulations.The following was observed during the inspection:A well plugging monument with the API number displayed was observed in the former location of the gas well (photos 19 and 20). No evidence of a spill to the surface, such as staining, was observed at the former well site location. No equipment related to well plugging and/or production was observed on site during this inspection. No evidence of nuisance mud tracking was observed from the site entrance onto Cutler Road (photo 1). The former access road and well site are temporarily stabilized and have established some vegetative growth since the time of IR 4181294, exhibiting approximately 40% vegetative growth coverage at the time of inspection. However, the third-party disturbances identified in IR 4181294 due livestock grazing continue to occur on site. The Department continues to recommend that the operator document any third-party disturbances occurring on site, and take reasonable efforts to stop them and prevent accelerated erosion from occurring on site. Temporary Erosion and sedimentation controls are installed downslope of the access road (photo 10). An access road cross-culvert is also protected by Compost Filter Sock (CFS). (photo 13) The site E and S/Restoration plans are available in a mailbox on site (photos 4-6). No evidence of accelerated erosion and sedimentation due to well plugging operations was observed on site during this inspection. However, some areas downslope of the former well site appear to lack the temporary E and S controls shown on the E and S plan drawing. Therefore, it appears that the operator continues to fail to follow the E and S control plan. Based on observations from this inspection, the violations issued in IR 4181294 shall remain outstanding. The Department recommends continued seeding and temporary stabilization on site until 70% uniform and adequate vegetative growth coverage is achieved. The violation issued in IR 4177612 for failure to post the API number on site shall be closed in IR 4205025.
